assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged oncology targets in human medicine, with 14 approved drugs spanning monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and small-molecule kinase inhibitors. Structural data is exceptionally rich (63 PDB entries, best resolution 1.25Å, multiple ligand-bound structures), and the chemical space is deeply explored with over 5,000 IC50 entries and a median potency of ~300 nM. Literature support is overwhelming with 2,443 title-level publications and active 2026 research across multiple cancer indications.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74.0 with only 66.8% high-confidence residues suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular linkers or flexible loops) not fully resolved in crystal structures — these regions may be relevant for novel binding modes

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., HER2 mutations, truncated p95-HER2, bypass signalling) are well-known but not captured in this summary — next-generation druggability for resistant tumours remains an active challenge
Non-oncology indications (e.g., cardiac toxicity, fibrosis as suggested by recent literature) are underexplored from a therapeutic standpoint
Selectivity profiling across the full ERBB family (EGFR, HER3, HER4) is not detailed here — pan-HER vs. selective inhibition trade-offs are clinically relevant
Biomarker stratification data (amplification vs. overexpression vs. mutation) and their correlation with drug response are not captured in the IC50 summary
